messages:
morgan: noticing a sudden p95 jump from FRA POP around 12:30UTC, ~3-4x baseline. throughput also dipped ~20%
alex: seeing same on dashboards — p50 stable, but p95/p99 spike, and overall QPS down. any deploys? :thinking:
priya: no deploys in the window. I pulled traces: tail of requests show large connect+first-byte RTTs for a subset of hosts in fra cluster.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-23185 - FRA POP latency spike (labels: runtime, kvcache, network)
morgan: ran a quick `dig` against our egress LDNS: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 fra.example-ldns` -> IPs returning are from new ASN (ASXYZ) vs usual AS12345.
alex: traceroute to one of the affected host IPs shows an extra 3-4 hops and >120ms jump at hop 7. `traceroute -n 185.54.x.y`
priya: kernel selector logs look noisy at same time: `kernel.selector: picked fallback-kernel for model-x (heuristic mismatch)`, repeated. seems selector flipped for ~30% of requests.
jamie: Could path change be causing CPU scheduling differences (more queuing) which pushes selector into fallback path?
morgan: hypothesis: provider path change increased RTTs -> batcher deadlines moved -> smaller batches -> more kernel switches -> KV cache miss amplification because requests hit cold hosts.
alex: profiled `batcher.latency_target_ms` behavior in that window: median batch size dropped from 12->4 for model-x. snippet from profiling: ```2026-03-12T12:31Z batch_sizes histogram: [4,5,4,3,4,6] active_batches: +32%```
priya: KV cache metrics: host-level kvcache hitrate fell 0.18 -> 0.05 on affected hosts. eviction rate spiked. looks like requests sharded differently across hosts now.
jamie: so two cascades: network path change -> increased per-request latency -> batching heuristic reduces batch sizes -> throughput down. plus traffic redistribution -> many cold kvcache misses -> p99 token generation slow.
morgan: I grabbed a perf sample from one affected runtime: `perf top` shows higher syscalls and context-switches while kernel fallback path has heavier memcopy ops. ```samples: 22% memcpy, 15% context-switch, 8% accept4```
alex: can we confirm provider announced a route change? checked BGP looking glass, saw a prepended route from ASXYZ ~12:28UTC.
priya: short mitigation idea: 1) pin kernel selector to `kernel-optimized` for fra for a few minutes 2) increase `batcher.latency_target_ms` from 12->25ms to allow larger batches 3) route fallback to alternative egress if available
morgan: applied kernel pin for fra POP: `redwoodctl runtime update --pop fra --kernel kernel-optimized --until 12m` — monitoring now.
ops-bot: config change recorded: CHG-9876 by morgan at 12:42UTC
jamie: bumped batcher target to 25ms via feature-flag for fraction of hosts (10%) to test, copy rolling now.
alex: within 3m after kernel pin + batch bump p95 dropped ~40%, throughput recovered ~10%. KV miss rate still high but trending down.
priya: digging into why selector flipped: selector uses measured CPU latency + observed batch size to pick kernel. because batch sizes shrank, math pushed score to fallback. we should make selector less sensitive to transient batch dip.
morgan: filed follow-up task: RUNTIME-424 - make kernel.selector windowing longer and add hysteresis so single-path jitter doesn't flip kernel. assigned to priya.
jamie: also an ops task: ROUTE-218 - add a egress-health check that detects sudden ASN changes and flags for runbook.
alex: long-term: consider warming kvcache on new hosts when traffic reshuffles (proactive prefetch) and add a cold-start grace policy to batching heuristics.
priya: capturing reproducible steps in incident doc (will paste link). one more datapoint: dig TTL across affected LDNS responses decreased which implies provider steering rather than sustained peering.
morgan: current status: p95 ~30% above baseline but trending to normal, ops mitigations holding. I'll keep the kernel pin until selector patch lands. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident INC-23185 status -> mitigated (monitoring).
